ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, PA and PB respectively tangent to the circle O at points A and B, point E is a point on the circle O, and $ \angle E=50^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $ \angle P$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect AO, BO,\\
$ \because $ PA and PB are tangents to circle O at points A and B, respectively,\\
$ \therefore \angle PAO=\angle PBO=90^\circ$\\
$ \because \angle E=50^\circ$\\
$ \therefore \angle AOB=2\angle E=100^\circ$\\
$ \therefore \angle P=360^\circ−\angle PAO−\angle PBO−\angle AOB=360^\circ−90^\circ−90^\circ−100^\circ=\boxed{80^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a circle, and the center of the circle is labeled O. Point A is at the upper right of the circle, point B is at the lower right of the circle, point P is on the right side of the circle, and PA and PB are tangent to the circle at points A and B respectively. Point E is on the left side of the circle, and two chords EA and EB are connected. Then reason: Because PA and PB are tangents, the radii OA and OB are respectively perpendicular to the tangents PA and PB, that is, ∠PAO=90° and ∠PBO=90°. In the figure, ∠E is ∠AEB=50°, and the central angle ∠AOB corresponding to the same arc AB that it subtends is 2×50°=100°. In quadrilateral AOPB, the sum of the interior angles is 360°, so ∠P=360°−90°−90°−100°=80°.
